q-161830.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224596/assets/fd18335a2034613658c65186c4fc6e3e74067e730183d3e66fbacf8ab3601928.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,z,\,-y⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
q-161830.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper paraboloid ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=z=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,R=-y.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-0\cdot (-2x)-(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot (-2y)+(-y))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(7y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨0,z,-y⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(7y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}8y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field F=⟨0,z,−y⟩ and the closed surface S that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
2x2y+2y3−8y
b
4y−2x2y−2y3
c
8y−2x2y−2y3
d
2x2y+2y3−6y
e
6y−2x2y−2y3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=4−x2−y2 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=0 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper paraboloid S1.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=g(x,y): ∂g∂x=∂∂x(4−x2−y2)=−2x∂g∂y=∂∂y(4−x2−y2)=−2y

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=0,Q=z=4−x2−y2,R=−y.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D(−0⋅(−2x)−(4−x2−y2)⋅(−2y)+(−y))dA=∬D(7y−2x2y−2y3)dA.

  • Consider the lower plane S2.

    Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,−1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=∬S2F⋅ndS=∬D⟨0,z,−y⟩⋅⟨0,0,−1⟩dA=∬DydA.

Therefore, the flux of F across the entire surface is

∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬D(7y−2x2y−2y3)dA+∬DydA=∬D8y−2x2y−2y3dA.

Consider the vector field $F=⟨-z,\,0,\,x⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
q-161895.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper paraboloid ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=-z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5,\,Q=0,\,R=x.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5)\cdot (-2x)-0\cdot (-2y)+x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{x}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}-10x+x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{x}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}-9x\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨-z,0,x⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-x\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2{x}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}-9x)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}-x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{x}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}-10x\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Consider the vector field F=⟨−z,0,x⟩ and the closed surface S that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
−4x3−2xy2+6x
b
2x3+2xy2−10x
c
2x3+4xy2−6x
d
4x3−4xy2+10x
e
−2x3−6xy2−6x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=5−x2−y2 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=0 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper paraboloid S1.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=g(x,y): ∂g∂x=∂∂x(5−x2−y2)=−2x∂g∂y=∂∂y(5−x2−y2)=−2y

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=−z=x2+y2−5,Q=0,R=x.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D−(x2+y2−5)⋅(−2x)−0⋅(−2y)+xdA=∬D2x3+2xy2−10x+xdA=∬D2x3+2xy2−9xdA.

  • Consider the lower plane S2.

    Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,−1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=∬S2F⋅ndS=∬D⟨−z,0,x⟩⋅⟨0,0,−1⟩dA=∬D−xdA.

Therefore, the flux of F across the entire surface is ∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬D(2x3+2xy2−9x)dA+∬D−xdA=∬D2x3+2xy2−10xdA.

q-161897.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224596/assets/6af3d84594e2b2648dcbbae05a64f03ef5a38c76f5a1ed835fc4c6b6f50ef97a.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,-x,\,-z⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}+\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-3\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
q-161897.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=3-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper cone ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=-x,\,R=-z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-3.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-0\cdot (-\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})-(-x)\cdot (-\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})+\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-3\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-3\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨0,-x,-0⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}0\,\text{d}A \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}-\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-3\,\text{d}A+0 \\  & ={∬}_{D}-\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-3\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the vector field F=⟨0,−x,−z⟩ and the closed surface S that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAA+x2+y2−3dA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
−xyx2+y2
b
xx2+y2
c
xyx2+y2
d
xyx2+y2
e
−xyx2+y2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=3−x2+y2 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=0 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper cone S1.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=g(x,y): ∂g∂x=∂∂x(3−x2+y2)=−xx2+y2∂g∂y=∂∂y(3−x2+y2)=−yx2+y2

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=0,Q=−x,R=−z=x2+y2−3.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D−0⋅(−xx2+y2)−(−x)⋅(−yx2+y2)+x2+y2−3dA=∬D−xyx2+y2+x2+y2−3dA.

  • Consider the lower plane S2.

    Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,−1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=∬S2F⋅ndS=∬D⟨0,−x,−0⟩⋅⟨0,0,−1⟩dA=∬D0dA=0.

Therefore, the flux of F across the entire surface is ∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬D−xyx2+y2+x2+y2−3dA+0=∬D−xyx2+y2+x2+y2−3dA.

q-161899.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224596/assets/8a48be0b4c101babf157a05959e923576ad5614113b3eec9e93fe747d5dc3803.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨1,\,x,\,0⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
q-161899.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper hemisphere ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}})=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}})=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=1,\,Q=x,\,R=0.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-1\cdot (-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}})-x\cdot (-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}})+0\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨1,x,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}0\,\text{d}A \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A+0 \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Consider the vector field F=⟨1,x,0⟩ and the closed surface S that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
x+xy1−x2−y2
b
xy−y1−x2−y2
c
xy1−x2−y2
d
x+y1−x2−y2
e
y−x1−x2−y2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=1−x2−y2 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=0 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper hemisphere S1.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=g(x,y): ∂g∂x=∂∂x(1−x2−y2)=−x1−x2−y2∂g∂y=∂∂y(1−x2−y2)=−y1−x2−y2

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=1,Q=x,R=0.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D−1⋅(−x1−x2−y2)−x⋅(−y1−x2−y2)+0dA=∬Dx+xy1−x2−y2dA.

  • Consider the lower plane S2.

    Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,−1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=∬S2F⋅ndS=∬D⟨1,x,0⟩⋅⟨0,0,−1⟩dA=∬D0dA=0.

Therefore, the flux of F across the entire surface is ∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬Dx+xy1−x2−y2dA+0=∬Dx+xy1−x2−y2dA.

q-161905.name: Question 5
q-161905.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=⟨z,\,0,\,y⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that encloses the finite region between the paraboloid $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5$ and the plane $z=0.$ Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
q-161905.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=0$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper plane ${S}_{1}.$

Since the positive orientation is upward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨z,0,y⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider lower paraboloid ${S}_{2}.$ 

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5)=2x \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5)=2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5,\,Q=0,\,R=y.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is downward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & =-{∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-5)\cdot (2x)-(0)\cdot (2y)+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-2{x}^{3}-2x{y}^{2}+10x+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{x}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}-10x-y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}2{x}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}-10x-y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{x}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}-10x\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the vector field F=⟨z,0,y⟩ and the closed surface S that encloses the finite region between the paraboloid z=x2+y2−5 and the plane z=0. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
 −2x3−2xy2+10x
b
 6x3+2xy2−10x−2y
c
2x3+2xy2−10x
d
 −2x3+4xy2+4x
e
 2x3+2xy2−5x+y
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=0 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=x2+y2−5 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper plane S1.

    Since the positive orientation is upward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬S1F⋅ndS=∬D⟨z,0,y⟩⋅⟨0,0,1⟩dA=∬DydA.

  • Consider lower paraboloid S2.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=h(x,y): ∂h∂x=∂∂x(x2+y2−5)=2x∂h∂y=∂∂y(x2+y2−5)=2y

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=z=x2+y2−5,Q=0,R=y.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is downward, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=−∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=−∬D(−(x2+y2−5)⋅(2x)−(0)⋅(2y)+y)dA=−∬D(−2x3−2xy2+10x+y)dA=∬D2x3+2xy2−10x−ydA.

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is

∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬DydA+∬D2x3+2xy2−10x−ydA=∬D2x3+2xy2−10xdA.
